chapter: Joining Raeburn and work for other leaders
title: Kenton's rehearsal crowd and Handy's unfinished score; Bob Gretinger
summary: Kenton told his players to hear Raeburn's rehearsals; Handy started a large concert score for Kenton but fell ill, and they discuss Bob Gretinger.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Kenton used to have his rehearsal and at the end of his rehearsal, he'd tell his guys to come down to our rehearsal to listen to what was happening. He said something new is
Did Kenton ask you to write for him?
Yeah. I still have a huge score, I thought I found it last night, but that wasn't it, the last thing I'd written for him, but I never got to him.
For which band?
His concert band.
The 1952 band, the one with the strings?
Right. It was a huge band, a very large band.
Bob Gretinger must have been writing for that band.
Right.
Did you know Bob?
No, I never met him, but I knew of him, I heard his work. He was an
excellent writer.

I assume this is true, it's been told to me and I've forgotten by whom, but someone I respect, Gretinger didn't write on score paper, he wrote on graph paper, he wrote in colored pencil, as I visualized it, something like some of that John Cage devices.
For Schillinger also.
Gretinger may have been a follower of Schillinger, but he wrote on graph paper.
I've never heard that.

He almost took vows of poverty and he would take twenty or thirty dollars a week from Stan and lived in a little room somewhere. Stan tried to give him more money and tried to get him to move into another house to break out of this, but he wanted to live that way. I don't know that, but it was told to me.
I would find no reason
to doubt anything like that; why not. People are different, one from the other.
That might have appealed to him.
As I said, I don't even know Bob, I don't know why he would have done something like that but I could certainly understand that people would do things like that.
What prevented your getting--to get back to the line--what prevented your getting that thing to the Kenton band?
Being sick.
Is it complete?
No, unfinished.

The first movement was complete and the second movement was--I think I was just about finished with the second movement. I may have needed a few more bars I think, but I had two more movements planned. But it was a long work. The first movement ran seven minutes or so.
Could the first two movements be performed independently? Would it
stand? Would you like to have that performed some time?
Where would I find a band that big?
